title: RAW UNREVIEWED: Atractylis entry excludes its thin root from a named aerial-part preparation
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED_NOT_SELECTED_NOT_TESTED. In the correctly bounded Lonitzer ATRACTYLIS entry (ff68r–68v), the morphological description calls the root 'tenuem et inutilem' (thin and useless). The following internal-use recipe names only leaves, coma, and seed, crushed with pepper and wine and taken against scorpion stings, attributed to Dioscorides. Preserve root versus recipe-part ownership: this historical wording does not put the root in that formulation. No broader claim that the root has no possible use is made.

whole_source.owner: ATRACTYLIS, ff68r–68v; explicitly before next heading CARDUUS, ff71r–72r
evidence: ATRACTYLIS description: 'florem pallidum, radicem tenuem et inutilem.'
ATRACTYLIS / VIRES, INTRINSECUS: 'Atractylidis folia, coma et semen, trita, cum pipere vinoque pota, contra scorpionum ictus prosunt, teste Dioscoride.'
whole_source.layer: CAMENA typed edition of Lonitzer, 1551, retained complete entries; not a fully corrected diplomatic transcription.

design.content_hypothesis: Within one entry, the source's explicitly named root is characterized as thin and useless, while a stated internal preparation identifies aerial materials (leaves, coma, seed) and pepper/wine as inputs. This creates a part-selection constraint; it does not prove the root is unusable for every purpose.
design.contrast: Keep the attributed scorpion-sting recipe attached to its written aerial inputs; do not substitute root or transfer the Carduus seed-shape clause from ff71r–72r into this entry.
design.smallest_next_authoring_object: If considered later, require a whole authorized target passage with independently fixed part and recipe-input roles. No target word or reading is supplied here.
strongest_limits: Exact source entry boundary and quote owner are stated above; the adjacent CARDUUS entry is not part of the evidence.
'Useless' is not expanded into an absolute, all-purpose exclusion beyond this written local contrast.
The recipe is attributed historical content, not an endorsed medical claim.
No target meaning or test is selected; duplicate retrieval is navigation only.
design.claim_ceiling: One source-grounded RAW_UNREVIEWED proposal; no target interpretation.
